decisions.quote: CALHM1 gene coding non-synonymous SNP P86L (rs2986017) was reported to increase the risk of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) in a recent study. Wehave investigated this genetic variant in 2470 individuals from Spain to conduct an independent replication study of the proposed SNP marker.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and the blind coder classify this study as a replication. The authors recruited and genotyped a new sample of 2,470 Spanish individuals to re-test the published association between the CALHM1 P86L polymorphism and Alzheimer's disease.

decisions.quote: Unfortunately, original ﬁndings, obtained in ﬁve different case-control series, were not replicated in a large-scale study of familial AD [2] and in six additional studies conducted in AD patients and controls from different populations (Sweden [2], Finland [2], Belgium [3], Caucasian Americans [4,5], and Asians [6]).
decisions.reason: Wrong original / non-target prior replication study. Reference [2] (Bertram et al., 2008, including the original authors' reply in Cell 135: 993-996) is explicitly introduced as an earlier replication study of the original findings [1] and included in the meta-analysis; its mention alongside [1, 4, 11] in Results serves to motivate testing [1]'s P86L variant under a recessive model for age at onset rather than establishing an independent replication target omitted by the shipped data.

decisions.reason: Wrong original / non-target prior replication study. Reference [4] (Minster et al., 2009) is explicitly introduced as one of the prior negative replication studies of the original findings [1] and is cited alongside [1, 2, 11] only as supporting the hypothetical recessive model for P86L in age at onset; per the codebook, an earlier replication attempt cited as background/context for model specification is not a separate target.

decisions.quote: Several independent research groups have observed that P86L and other CALMH1 markers modulate the AAO only under a recessive model [1,2,4,11]. These observations reinforce a hypothetical recessive model for the P86L variant in AD. So, we decided to evaluate this model in AAO in Spanish AD patients.
decisions.reason: Wrong original / background citation. Reference [11] (Li et al., 2008) is cited only once in passing as part of the background observation that 'P86L and other CALMH1 markers modulate the AAO only under a recessive model [1,2,4,11]' to motivate evaluating the recessive model for P86L in the authors' replication of [1]; the present paper only genotyped P86L and P85P and did not re-test Li et al.'s GWAS candidate SNPs.

decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and blind target 0 identify Reference [1], Dreses-Werringloer et al. (2008, Cell 133, 1149-1161; DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2008.05.048), as the original study that proposed the CALHM1 P86L (rs2986017) polymorphism in Alzheimer's disease risk and age at onset. The competing blind targets [2], [4], and [11] are prior replication studies of [1] or background literature cited to motivate evaluating the recessive model for age at onset rather than independent tested originals.

decisions.reason: With original identity resolved to Dreses-Werringloer et al. (2008) [1] (target_index 0), both the shipped record and blind target 0 agree on a mixed outcome. The authors report a full independent replication of the P86L effect on age at onset in LOAD (p = 0.002, surviving Bonferroni correction and covariate adjustment, though absent in EOAD) and only weak/nominal case-control association in LOAD (OR = 1.381, p = 0.042, which does not survive covariate adjustment or Bonferroni correction), while explicitly contrasting the recessive genetic model observed in their Spanish sample with the dominant model originally proposed in [1].

prior_decision.quote: Both results are compatible with the original ﬁndings [1], although the observed genetic model for the P86L mutation in Spanish series seems different. In fact, we observed a recessive instead a dominant model as originally proposed.
prior_decision.reason: Both the shipped record and blind target 0 code the outcome for Dreses-Werringloer et al. (2008) as mixed. The authors report nominal/weak case-control association in LOAD (which does not survive covariate adjustment or Bonferroni correction) and replicate the age-at-onset (AAO) effect in LOAD (but not EOAD), while explicitly contrasting the recessive genetic model observed in their Spanish series with the dominant model originally proposed in [1].
